subject: Environment
description: Covers WPA 1972 schedules, NTCA, NBWL, WCCB, and recent amendments.

questions.stem: The Wildlife (Protection) Act of 1972 originally had six schedules. Following the 2022 Amendment, how many schedules does the Act currently have?

options.option_text: 4 schedules
6 schedules
8 schedules
2 schedules

questions.explanation:
WPA AMENDMENT 2022: Rationalized the schedules from 6 to 4 to simplify the act.
- Schedule I: Highest protection (strict penalties) for endangered species (e.g., Tiger, Elephant).
- Schedule II: Lesser degree of protection.
- Schedule III: Protected Plant species (formerly Sch VI).
- Schedule IV: Specimens listed in CITES (newly added to implement CITES obligations). 
The old "Vermin" schedule (Sch V) was removed, though states can still declare species as vermin. PYQ FREQUENCY: Current Affairs & Env GS-3.

questions.stem: Which authority is constituted under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 to manage the network of Tiger Reserves in India?

options.option_text: National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)
Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB)
Animal Welfare Board of India (AWBI)
National Board for Wildlife (NBWL)

questions.explanation: NTCA (National Tiger Conservation Authority): A statutory body under the MoEFCC, established in 2005 following the recommendations of the Tiger Task Force. It was given statutory status via a 2006 amendment to the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. It oversees Project Tiger (launched 1973) and manages Tiger Reserves. The WCCB is also statutory under WPA (amended 2006) for combating organized wildlife crime. The AWBI is statutory under the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960. PYQ FREQUENCY: UPSC Prelims, State PSCs.

questions.stem: Under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, who is the statutory chairperson of the National Board for Wildlife (NBWL)?

options.option_text: The Prime Minister of India
The Minister of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
The Director General of Forests
A retired Supreme Court Judge appointed by the President

questions.explanation:
NATIONAL BOARD FOR WILDLIFE (NBWL): A statutory organization constituted under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. It serves as the apex body to review all wildlife-related matters and approve projects in and around national parks and sanctuaries. 
- CHAIRPERSON: Prime Minister of India.
- VICE CHAIRPERSON: Minister of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
State Boards for Wildlife are chaired by the respective Chief Ministers. PYQ FREQUENCY: UPSC Prelims (very frequently tested), SSC CGL.

questions.stem: If a species is listed in Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, it implies that:

options.option_text: It is accorded the highest level of protection, and poaching or trading it incurs the severest penalties
It is a vermin species that can be hunted freely without restriction
It is an invasive alien species marked for eradication
It can only be hunted with a permit from the Chief Wildlife Warden for commercial purposes

questions.explanation: SCHEDULE I OF WPA 1972: Covers endangered species that require rigorous protection. Offences under Schedule I attract the highest penalties (imprisonment from 3 to 7 years and fines). Examples: Tiger, Snow Leopard, Great Indian Bustard, Gangetic Dolphin, Whale Shark. Hunting is absolutely prohibited except under extremely rare conditions (like threat to human life or for scientific research), and only with explicit permission from the Chief Wildlife Warden. PYQ FREQUENCY: UPSC Prelims, IFS, State PSCs.

questions.stem: Which statutory body, created under a 2006 amendment to the Wildlife (Protection) Act, is mandated to combat organized wildlife crime networks across India?

options.option_text: Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB)
Central Bureau of Investigation - Wildlife Wing (CBI-WW)
National Green Tribunal (NGT)
Forest Survey of India (FSI)

questions.explanation: WILDLIFE CRIME CONTROL BUREAU (WCCB): A statutory multi-disciplinary body established in 2007 (under the 2006 amendment to the WPA 1972). It gathers intelligence on organized wildlife crime, assists states in successful prosecutions, implements obligations under CITES, and sets up centralized wildlife crime databanks. Headquartered in New Delhi. NGT was created under the NGT Act 2010. FSI is under MoEFCC but is not a law enforcement agency. PYQ FREQUENCY: UPSC Prelims, UPPSC.

questions.stem: The power to declare any wild animal (other than those in Schedule I and II) as "vermin" for a specific period and area under the Wildlife (Protection) Act rests with:

options.option_text: The Central Government
The State Government
The Chief Wildlife Warden of the State
The National Board for Wildlife

questions.explanation: VERMIN DECLARATION: Section 62 of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 empowers the CENTRAL GOVERNMENT to declare any wild animal (other than those specified in Schedule I and Schedule II) as "vermin" for any area and for a specified period. Once declared vermin, the animal is deprived of its protection under the Act and can be hunted. States send requests (e.g., Bihar for Nilgai, Himachal for Rhesus Macaque), but the notification must be issued by the Centre. PYQ FREQUENCY: UPSC Prelims GS-3, State PSCs.

questions.stem: Community Reserves and Conservation Reserves, categories of protected areas acting as buffer zones or connectors, were introduced into the Wildlife (Protection) Act by an amendment in:
questions.explanation:
CONSERVATION & COMMUNITY RESERVES: Introduced via the Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2002. 
- CONSERVATION RESERVES: Declared by the State Gov on government-owned lands (usually adjacent to NPs/Sanctuaries) after consulting local communities.
- COMMUNITY RESERVES: Declared on private or community lands where the community volunteers to conserve wildlife. Both serve as vital flexible buffer zones and migration corridors. Tiruppadaimarathur in Tamil Nadu was India's first Conservation Reserve. PYQ FREQUENCY: UPSC Prelims, IFS Forestry.

questions.stem: After the Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022 restructured the schedule list, which schedule now governs the protection of specified plants under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972?

options.option_text: Schedule I, which covers all specially protected species including fauna and flora
Schedule II, which exclusively lists specified protected plant species
Schedule III, which covers specimens listed under CITES appendices
Schedule IV, which consolidates vermin and plant species together

questions.explanation: The 2022 amendment reduced the schedules from 6 to 4. Schedule II now covers specified plants (previously under Schedule VI of the unamended Act). Schedule I covers specially protected animals, Schedule III covers CITES-listed specimens, and Schedule IV lists vermin. Option A is wrong because Schedule I is restricted to specially protected animals, not plants.

questions.stem: Under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, what is the most significant legal distinction between a National Park and a Wildlife Sanctuary regarding the rights of local people?

options.option_text: Local rights are fully extinguished in both National Parks and Sanctuaries
A Sanctuary may permit livestock grazing; a National Park allows no rights at all
National Parks are Central-government-notified; Sanctuaries are state-notified
Habitat destruction for tribal settlements is permitted in Sanctuaries but not National Parks

questions.explanation: Section 26A of WPA empowers the Chief Wildlife Warden to permit grazing or movement of livestock inside a Wildlife Sanctuary. National Parks (Section 35) are categorically stricter — no rights of any person can be exercised inside. Both PA types are notified by State Governments, making Option C incorrect. Option A is wrong as Sanctuary rights are not automatically extinguished — they may be regulated or permitted.

questions.stem: Under Section 51(1A) of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, what is the minimum prescribed punishment for a first-time conviction for hunting a wild animal listed in Schedule I?

options.option_text: Simple imprisonment of one year with a fine not exceeding ₹10,000
Rigorous imprisonment of three years (up to seven), plus a minimum fine of ₹25,000
Rigorous imprisonment of seven years extendable to life, with no minimum fine cap
Imprisonment of two years with mandatory forfeiture of the vehicle used

questions.explanation: Section 51(1A) prescribes a minimum of 3 years' rigorous imprisonment (extendable to 7 years) and a minimum fine of ₹25,000 for offences involving Schedule I species. Option C — life imprisonment — applies only to repeat offenders (second or subsequent conviction), not first-time convictions. Option D's two-year term is the general fallback for less serious offences.

questions.stem: The Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022 inserted Schedule III into the Act to give direct domestic legal effect to India's obligations under which international treaty?

options.option_text: Ramsar Convention on Wetlands of International Importance (wetland treaty)
Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species (CITES) appendices
UN Convention on Biological Diversity's Nagoya Protocol on access and benefit sharing
Bonn Convention on Migratory Species of Wild Animals (CMS)

questions.explanation: The 2022 amendment introduced Schedule III specifically to list specimens regulated under CITES (Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora), aligning domestic law with India's trade-control obligations at the border. The Ramsar Convention (Option A) deals with wetland designation, not wildlife trade; the Nagoya Protocol (Option C) governs genetic resource access — a common distractor in biodiversity questions.

questions.stem: The Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife (NBWL), which examines proposals for development projects inside or adjacent to Protected Areas, is chaired by whom under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972?

options.option_text: The Prime Minister of India, who chairs the full NBWL board
The Union Minister in charge of Forests and Environment
The Director General of Forests and Special Secretary (Wildlife)
The Chief Justice of India or a Supreme Court nominee designated for the role

questions.explanation: The Standing Committee of NBWL, which clears project proposals in and around PAs, is chaired by the Union Minister of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. The Prime Minister chairs the full NBWL (not the Standing Committee) — a distinction frequently tested in SSC and IBPS exams. Option C describes a senior forest bureaucrat who serves as member-secretary, not chairperson.

questions.stem: Before a State Government can notify an area as 'Critical Tiger Habitat' (core zone) under Section 38V(4) of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, which condition is a mandatory statutory precondition?

options.option_text: Consent of at least two-thirds of tribal gram sabhas within the proposed core zone
Expert committee's scientific finding that co-existence with human activity is not possible
Prior NTCA approval before any expert committee can be constituted by the state
Central Government gazette notification permitting the state to initiate the process

questions.explanation: Section 38V(4) requires an expert committee comprising ecologists, wildlife biologists, and local community representatives to scientifically determine that co-existence with human activity in the identified area is not possible before it is notified as Critical Tiger Habitat. Option A conflates this with Forest Rights Act, 2006 obligations — FRA requires rights to be settled before relocation, but does not mandate gram sabha consent as a precondition under WPA. Options C and D have no basis in the statutory text.

questions.stem: Under Chapter IVB of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, a recognised zoo seeking to acquire a live wild animal from a foreign zoo must obtain permission from which authority, and this transfer simultaneously mandates compliance with which international instrument?

options.option_text: State Chief Wildlife Warden's permit; compliance with Ramsar Convention listing norms
CZA recognition + Director (Wildlife Preservation) permit; CITES documentation required
NBWL approval; compliance with the Convention on Migratory Species (Bonn Convention)
State forest department permit; compliance with IUCN Red List reclassification criteria

questions.explanation: Chapter IVB (inserted in 1991) places zoo regulation under the Central Zoo Authority (CZA), and international transfers of wild animals require approval from the Director (Wildlife Preservation) in addition to CZA recognition. Since many zoo species appear on CITES appendices, valid CITES export/import permits are compulsory. The IUCN Red List (Option D) is a conservation assessment tool, not a treaty; the Bonn Convention (Option C) governs migratory species, not captive zoo acquisitions.
